newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News shares slide after ADRs' dive.
newsitem.headline: News shares slide after ADRs' dive.

text.p: Shares in the Rupert Murdoch-controlled News Corporation Ltd shed nearly three percent to an intraday low of A$5.88 on Monday as local traders factored in a sharp falls in News ADRs in U.S. trade last week.
Talk of a delayed release of the movie feature, "Titanic", reputedly the most expensive ever made, also softened sentiment towards the multi-media giant.
News ADRs tumbled over three percent last Thursday, falling to US$18-1/8, before rallying slightly to US$18-3/8 on Friday. The Australian market was closed on Friday for the ANZAC day public holiday.

"It's a combination - we are catching up with several days trade but they are also talking about the 'Titanic' movie not being released on the Fourth of July in the U.S.," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage, alluding to preferred premiere date of major U.S. movies over the North American summer.
"One of the most expensive movies ever made looks like being delayed."
By 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), News Corp shares were 14 cents lower at A$5.91 on turnover of 3.8 million shares, a volume that was boosted by the exercise of April series options.
